title: Foreground Execution Durability and Interruption Circuit Breaker
owner_directive: Wire the repeated browser-freeze, overhandling, polling, stale-recovery, and lane-monopolization failure pattern into OPS4 so future agents fail safe instead of repeating it.
reproduced_failure: Across multiple Multiversal conversations, long synchronous browser turns accumulated dozens of repository/CI/tool actions and repeatedly ended in browser freeze, connection interruption, or stopped thinking before a clean response.
After interruption, recovery often expanded into broad repository archaeology and repeated CI inspection, creating more tool traffic and another interruption.
Foreground sessions sometimes held execution context across external waits, polled workflows, or prepared later same-branch tasks while an earlier immutable candidate was still under acceptance.
Durable repository state frequently advanced beyond the visible conversation, forcing the owner to repeatedly ask where execution got to and creating stale-checkpoint or under-reporting incidents.
research_basis: Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents (2025): long-running agents lose session context, need incremental progress, git/progress artifacts, and clean handoffs.

OpenAI, Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world (2026): reliable coding agents use isolated worktrees, local tools, executable feedback loops, repository-local plans, and enforceable invariants.
OpenAI API Background mode: long-running tasks should run asynchronously so connectivity/timeouts do not own execution lifetime.
Temporal + OpenAI Agents SDK durable execution: long-running agent work should resume after crashes/network loss rather than restart.
LangGraph durable execution/interrupt: persist graph state at every step so interrupted work resumes from checkpoints.
Microsoft Circuit Breaker pattern and AWS retry guidance: repeated calls to failing/slow dependencies should be bounded; stop retry storms and fail safe.
decisions: Foreground chat is a bounded supervisor/worker quantum, not the persistence layer for multi-hour implementation.
A foreground quantum is capped at 6 tool batches and 18 remote operations.
One CI observation per candidate per foreground quantum; terminal failure permits one failed-job and one first-failure log inspection.
Sleep/wait/poll loops are forbidden in foreground execution.
Interruption recovery defaults to four durable surfaces and requires a resume capsule at every wait/interruption/budget boundary.
Same-branch next-task mutations are forbidden while the current immutable candidate is under CI; independent work must be read-only or isolated elsewhere.
Foreground execution leases release at waits and response boundaries.

Two foreground interruptions on one attempt open a circuit breaker; product implementation cannot continue in browser foreground until moved to durable/background execution or an owner-approved harness repair resets the circuit.
